chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Fronting the band for T-Bone Walker, Pee Wee Crayton and others
summary: Smith's band backed visiting blues acts like T-Bone Walker, Pee Wee Crayton, Roy Hawkins and Jimmy Witherspoon; no recording happened because studios were far.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah, yeah. See, it was my group. I had to keep a band together. So I just made them dates with him, just like I did... See, when I wasn't with him, T-Bone would come in town...

Yeah. And I'd go with him. And when it wasn't him, I was out with Pee Wee Crayton. We'd take the same band out with him.. Then Roy Hawkins. I'd take the same band. And with the other boy, Jimmy... I went out with Jimmy Witherspoon one time. Then I went out with another boy who came in named Jimmy. All them little acts like that, that come out here -- singers and
Jimmy... What's that other boy? He's down here in San Antonio now. His name is Jimmy, too. I can't tell you...
Yeah. I can't think of his last name right now. He's out there in San Antonio. No, he's in Corpus Christi.
Did you ever record with T-Bone?
No. T-Bone always made his records out there...
Yeah, in L.A. there. And he used that little boy who got that little seven or eight piece band there in Los Angeles. (?)Jimmy Wynn(?).

I heard some records T-Bone made in the late '40s and the early 50's. And he had a little band, a tenor... Or it might have been alto. I think tenor, trumpet and rhythm section and T-Bone. And I tell you, you would have blown that tenor player out of the room.
It's a pity he didn't use you.

Yeah, well, Jimmy Wynn(?) and them, and all them out there, he did a lot of arranging for them. He wrote a lot of arrangements them for small groups like that. And he was out there, and I think he played tenor or something. Anyway, it would have cost too much money to transfer my band out there, and we didn't have no recording studio here at all. The only one,
the closest one was over there in Fort Worth, and there wasn't nobody that had nothing to offer. And he wouldn't take no chance with them.
